BANTAY-TB: A GIS-Based Spatial Surveillance and Hotspot Detection System for Tuberculosis in Davao City

BANTAY-TB is a web-based tuberculosis surveillance platform for the Davao City Health Office that records TB cases and shows, barangay by barangay, where TB burden is statistically concentrated across the city's 182 barangays. Health staff add, edit or bulk-import cases from Excel files laid out like the DOH Form 6a DS-TB Register; each case is attributed to its barangay of residence using PSGC codes. A server-side hotspot job counts cases per barangay over a configurable window, converts them to cases per 100,000 population using PSA census denominators, tests for global clustering with Moran's I (row-standardised queen contiguity weights, 999 permutations), and computes a local Getis-Ord Gi* z-score for every barangay. Barangays significant at 95% or 99% are classified as high or urgent hotspots and shown on an interactive GIS map with a heatmap layer and plain-language reasons. Only barangays that newly become hotspots trigger alerts, which are routed by residence: city-wide roles (TB coordinator, system administrator) receive every alert, while barangay staff are alerted only when their own residents are in the cluster. Residents use public pages without an account: a DOTS center locator that ranks treatment facilities by distance from the user's geolocation and shows a route, plain-language health guides, and a chatbot that detects English, Filipino (Tagalog) or Cebuano and answers only from a reviewed knowledge base (retrieval-augmented generation), with a fixed out-of-scope reply and no diagnosis. Case records can be exported as HL7 FHIR R4 transaction bundles to an allow-listed endpoint, with each attempt written to a hash-chained, append-only audit log. Staff accounts are created only through single-use invite codes, and row-level security limits each role to its assigned area or facility. Stack: React + TypeScript + Vite, Leaflet / MapLibre GL; Supabase (PostgreSQL, Auth, Edge Functions).

No granted patent or published application was located that is directed to tuberculosis hotspot detection over barangay-level (or comparable village-level) administrative units using Getis-Ord Gi*. The patent documents retrieved address general infectious-disease surveillance: scan-statistic cluster detection with map display and SMS/e-mail warnings (CN103310083B), threshold-based anomaly detection with escalating alerts and multilingual access (US9727702B2), and region-level spot maps with automatic flagging of suspicious events (US8626521B2). TB-specific web GIS appears only in the non-patent literature (Portal TB Gombak), and the exact statistics BANTAY-TB uses (Moran's I, Getis-Ord Gi*, queen weights) are long public in ArcGIS, GeoDa and the literature.

The individual mechanisms BANTAY-TB uses are therefore each disclosed somewhere in the art, and the statistics themselves are public mathematical methods. Any argument for novelty and inventive step must rest on the specific combination as implemented: Gi* classification gated by a global Moran's I test on population-normalised barangay rates; alerts raised only for barangays that newly become hotspots and routed by the patients' barangay of residence to jurisdiction-scoped staff; the public DOTS locator; the English / Filipino / Cebuano chatbot answering only from a reviewed knowledge base; and FHIR R4 export with a hash-chained audit log. Note also that the Philippine IP Code (R.A. 8293, Section 22) excludes mathematical methods and programs for computers as such from patentability, so the team should confirm with the UIC IP office whether a patent, utility model or copyright registration is the right protection route.
